title: Three trial-entry deletions can reverse a selected worm electrical cycle imbalance
abstract: We tested the sensitivity of a published worm response cycle to removal of exported trial entries. The sample linked a pooled wild-type signal atlas to electrical contacts in either of two adult anatomy maps. Its 21 pairs had one independent cycle. The cycle used eight response lists with 272 entries and had a signed log sum of -0.630019. Exact finite optimization showed that no deletion of one or two entries can reverse its sign. Three entries from one direction can give +0.082777. These are 1.10 percent of the pooled entries but 13.04 percent of that direction. Exhaustive checks of 272 single and 36,856 double deletions confirmed the bounds. All eight list means matched the stored response means, but stored occurrence counts summed to 318 rather than 272. Selection stayed fixed after deletion. The result is a sensitivity audit, not evidence for wrong trials, exact reciprocity or electrical rectification. Missing event and animal IDs, pooled calcium responses and anatomy from other animals limit inference. Original code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and external retrieval steps support reproduction.

display.caption: Exact smallest and largest cycle sums at fixed deletion budgets. Three selected entries can reverse the sign. The graph and response selection stay fixed.
